topic: Task-Based versus Thread-Based: The Default Recommendation
explanation: Assumption: Direct use of `std::thread` provides the most control and is the standard way to achieve concurrency. Reality: For most common use cases, task-based programming using `std::async` is superior and recommended. Why It Fails: Raw `std::thread` requires manual management of thread exhaustion, oversubscription, load balancing, and platform adaptation. Task-based programming (with the default launch policy) handles these resource management issues automatically, making concurrent code safer and more portable.
practical_example: A developer needs to run 10 short, independent calculation tasks. Using 10 raw `std::thread` objects risks oversubscribing the system or requiring complex manual thread pool management. Using 10 `std::async` calls allows the runtime to efficiently manage thread allocation and reuse, improving overall system stability.
chapter: Item 35: Prefer task-based programming to thread-based programming
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
